function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in the context of financial services (especially mutual funds, ETFs, or other investment products) refers to an official authorization or instruction that allows a fund manager or investment platform to act on behalf of an investor. It typically includes:

| Element | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Client Authorization** | The investor gives explicit permission for the platform or fund manager to manage their investments. |
| **Investment Scope** | Specifies which funds or securities the manager can invest in, and any limits or restrictions. |
| **Duration & Status** | Mandates can be *active*, *pending*, or *inactive*. An active mandate means the manager can transact; pending indicates it’s awaiting approval; inactive means it has been terminated or paused. |
| **Compliance & Reporting** | Mandates ensure that all transactions comply with regulatory requirements and that investors receive regular performance reports. |

In practice, when you open an account with a mutual‑fund distributor or a robo‑advisor, they will issue a mandate that authorizes them to buy, sell, or rebalance your holdings according to your chosen strategy. This legal document protects both the investor and the service provider by clearly defining responsibilities and limits.
